57:    */

67:   int retry;

69:   if ((unsigned int)cpu >= CONFIG_SMP_NCPUS || cpu == this_cpu())

74:   atomic_or_release(&g_ipi_pending[cpu], pending);
75:   if (!atomic_cmpxchg_acquire(&g_ipi_kicked[cpu], &expected, 1))

97:     }

163:         }

166:     }

137: /****************************************************************************
138:  * Name: spin_lock_notrace
139:  *
140:  * Description:
141:  *   If this CPU does not already hold the spinlock, then loop until the
142:  *   spinlock is successfully locked.
143:  *
144:  *   This implementation is the same as the above spin_lock() except that
145:  *   it does not perform instrumentation logic.
146:  *
147:  * Input Parameters:
148:  *   lock - A reference to the spinlock object to lock.
149:  *
150:  * Returned Value:
151:  *   None.  When the function returns, the spinlock was successfully locked
152:  *   by this CPU.
153:  *
154:  * Assumptions:
155:  *   Not running at the interrupt level.
156:  *
157:  ****************************************************************************/
158: 
159: #ifdef CONFIG_SPINLOCK
160: static inline_function noinstrument_function
161: void spin_lock_notrace(FAR volatile spinlock_t *lock)
162: {
163: #ifdef CONFIG_TICKET_SPINLOCK
164:   int ticket = atomic_add_relaxed(&lock->next, 1);
165:   while (atomic_read_acquire(&lock->owner) != ticket);
166: #else /* CONFIG_TICKET_SPINLOCK */
167:   while (atomic_xchg_acquire(&lock->lock, 1) == 1);
168: #endif
169: }
170: #else
171: #  define spin_lock_notrace(lock) ((void)(lock))
172: #endif /* CONFIG_SPINLOCK */

174: /****************************************************************************
175:  * Name: spin_lock
176:  *
177:  * Description:
178:  *   If this CPU does not already hold the spinlock, then loop until the
179:  *   spinlock is successfully locked.
180:  *
181:  *   This implementation is non-reentrant and is prone to deadlocks in
182:  *   the case that any logic on the same CPU attempts to take the lock
183:  *   more than once.
184:  *
185:  * Input Parameters:
186:  *   lock - A reference to the spinlock object to lock.
187:  *
188:  * Returned Value:
189:  *   None.  When the function returns, the spinlock was successfully locked
190:  *   by this CPU.
191:  *
192:  * Assumptions:
193:  *   Not running at the interrupt level.
194:  *
195:  ****************************************************************************/
196: 
197: #ifdef CONFIG_SPINLOCK
198: static inline_function void spin_lock(FAR volatile spinlock_t *lock)
199: {
200:   /* Mark that we want to hold lock */
201: 
202:   spinlock_mark_locking(&lock->info);
203: 
204:   /* Notify that we are waiting for a spinlock */
205: 
206:   sched_note_spinlock(lock, NOTE_SPINLOCK_LOCK);
207: 
208:   /* If CONFIG_SCHED_CRITMONITOR_MAXTIME_BUSYWAIT >= 0, count busy-waiting. */
209: 
210:   nxsched_critmon_busywait(true, return_address(0));
211: 
212:   /* Lock without trace note */
213: 
214:   spin_lock_notrace(lock);
215: 
216:   /* Mark the spinlock has been locked */
217: 
218:   spinlock_mark_locked(&lock->info);
219: 
220:   /* Get the lock, end counting busy-waiting */
221: 
222:   nxsched_critmon_busywait(false, return_address(0));
223: 
224:   /* Notify that we have the spinlock */
225: 
226:   sched_note_spinlock(lock, NOTE_SPINLOCK_LOCKED);
227: }
228: #else
229: #  define spin_lock(lock) ((void)(lock))
230: #endif /* CONFIG_SPINLOCK */

232: /****************************************************************************
233:  * Name: spin_trylock_notrace
234:  *
235:  * Description:
236:  *   Try once to lock the spinlock.  Do not wait if the spinlock is already
237:  *   locked.
238:  *
239:  *   This implementation is the same as the above spin_trylock() except that
240:  *   it does not perform instrumentation logic.
241:  *
242:  * Input Parameters:
243:  *   lock - A reference to the spinlock object to lock.
244:  *
245:  * Returned Value:
246:  *   false - Failure, the spinlock was already locked
247:  *   true  - Success, the spinlock was successfully locked
248:  *
249:  * Assumptions:
250:  *   Not running at the interrupt level.
251:  *
252:  ****************************************************************************/
253: 
254: #ifdef CONFIG_SPINLOCK
255: static inline_function noinstrument_function bool
256: spin_trylock_notrace(FAR volatile spinlock_t *lock)
257: {
258: #ifdef CONFIG_TICKET_SPINLOCK
259:   atomic_t expected = atomic_read(&lock->owner);
260:   atomic_t next = expected + 1;
261: 
262:   /* Keep the expected value private.  A failed compare-exchange updates its
263:    * expected argument; passing &lock->owner would corrupt the ticket owner. */
264:   return atomic_cmpxchg_acquire(&lock->next, &expected, next);
265: #else /* CONFIG_TICKET_SPINLOCK */
266:   return atomic_xchg_acquire(&lock->lock, 1) != 1;
267: #endif /* CONFIG_TICKET_SPINLOCK */
268: }
269: #else
270: #  define spin_trylock_notrace(lock) ((void)(lock), true)
271: #endif /* CONFIG_SPINLOCK */

273: /****************************************************************************
274:  * Name: spin_trylock
275:  *
276:  * Description:
277:  *   Try once to lock the spinlock.  Do not wait if the spinlock is already
278:  *   locked.
279:  *
280:  * Input Parameters:
281:  *   lock - A reference to the spinlock object to lock.
282:  *
283:  * Returned Value:
284:  *   false - Failure, the spinlock was already locked
285:  *   true  - Success, the spinlock was successfully locked
286:  *
287:  * Assumptions:
288:  *   Not running at the interrupt level.
289:  *
290:  ****************************************************************************/
291: 
292: #ifdef CONFIG_SPINLOCK
293: static inline_function bool spin_trylock(FAR volatile spinlock_t *lock)
294: {
295:   bool locked;
296: 
297:   /* Notify that we are waiting for a spinlock */
298: 
299:   sched_note_spinlock(lock, NOTE_SPINLOCK_LOCK);
300: 
301:   /* Try lock without trace note */
302: 
303:   locked = spin_trylock_notrace(lock);
304:   if (locked)
305:     {
306:       /* Mark the spinlock has been locked */
307: 
308:       spinlock_mark_locked(&lock->info);
309: 
310:       /* Notify that we have the spinlock */
311: 
312:       sched_note_spinlock(lock, NOTE_SPINLOCK_LOCKED);
313:     }
314:   else
315:     {
316:       /* Notify that we abort for a spinlock */
317: 
318:       sched_note_spinlock(lock, NOTE_SPINLOCK_ABORT);
319:     }
320: 
321:   return locked;
322: }
323: #else
324: #  define spin_trylock(lock) ((void)(lock), true)
325: #endif /* CONFIG_SPINLOCK */

640: /****************************************************************************
641:  * Name: rspin_lock/rspin_lock_irqsave/rspin_lock_irqsave_nopreempt
642:  *
643:  * Description:
644:  *   Nest supported spinlock, can support UINT16_MAX max depth.
645:  *   As we should not disable irq for long time, sched also locked.
646:  *   Similar feature with enter_critical_section, but isolate by instance.
647:  *
648:  *   If SPINLOCK is enabled:
649:  *     Will take spinlock each cpu first call.
650:  *
651:  *   If SPINLOCK is not enabled:
652:  *     Equivalent to up_irq_save() + sched_lock().
653:  *     Will only sched_lock once when first called.
654:  *
655:  *   NOTE: This function is only allowed to execute with irq disabled.
656:  *
657:  * Input Parameters:
658:  *   lock - Caller specific rspinlock_s. not NULL.
659:  *
660:  * Returned Value:
661:  *   An opaque, architecture-specific value that represents the state of
662:  *   the interrupts prior to the call to spin_lock_irqsave(lock);
663:  *
664:  ****************************************************************************/
665: 
666: #ifdef CONFIG_SPINLOCK
667: static inline_function
668: void rspin_lock(FAR rspinlock_t *lock)
669: {
670:   rspinlock_t new_val;
671:   rspinlock_t old_val;
672:   int         cpu = this_cpu() + 1;
673: 
674:   /* Already owned this lock. */
675: 
676:   old_val.val = atomic_read(&lock->val);
677: 
678:   if (old_val.owner == cpu)
679:     {
680:       lock->count += 1;
681:     }
682:   else
683:     {
684:       /* Mark that we want to hold lock */
685: 
686:       spinlock_mark_locking(&lock->info);
687: 
688:       /* Try seize the ownership of the lock using CAS. */
689: 
690:       new_val.count = 1;
691:       new_val.owner = cpu;
692: 
693:       do
694:         {
695:           old_val.val = 0;
696:         }
697:       while (!atomic_cmpxchg_acquire(&lock->val,
698:              &old_val.val, new_val.val));
699: 
700:       /* Mark locked only when the lock is acquired for the first time. */
701: 
702:       spinlock_mark_locked(&lock->info);
703:     }
704: }
705: 
706: static inline_function
707: irqstate_t rspin_lock_irqsave(FAR rspinlock_t *lock)
708: {
709:   irqstate_t flags = up_irq_save();
710:   rspin_lock(lock);
711: 
712:   return flags;
713: }
714: #else
715: static inline_function
716: irqstate_t rspin_lock_irqsave(FAR rspinlock_t *lock)
717: {
718:   irqstate_t flags = up_irq_save();
719:   lock->count++;
720:   lock->owner = this_cpu() + 1;
721:   return flags;
722: }
723: #endif
724: 
725: static inline_function
726: irqstate_t rspin_lock_irqsave_nopreempt(FAR rspinlock_t *lock)
727: {
728:   irqstate_t flags;
729:   flags = rspin_lock_irqsave(lock);
730:   sched_lock();
731:   return flags;
732: }

735:  * Name: rspin_trylock/rspin_trylock_irqsave/rspin_trylock_irqsave_nopreempt

737:  * Description:

739:  *   UINT16_MAX max depth.
740:  *   As we should not disable irq for long time, sched also locked.
741:  *   Similar feature with enter_critical_section, but isolate by instance.
742:  *
743:  *   If SPINLOCK is enabled:
744:  *     Will take spinlock each cpu first call.
745:  *
746:  *   If SPINLOCK is not enabled:
747:  *     Equivalent to up_irq_save() + sched_lock().
748:  *     Will only sched_lock once when first called.
749:  *
750:  * Input Parameters:
751:  *   lock - Caller specific rspinlock_s. not NULL.
752:  *
753:  * Returned Value:
754:  *   true  - Success, the spinlock was successfully locked
755:  *   false - Failure, the spinlock was already locked
756:  *

759: #ifdef CONFIG_SPINLOCK
760: static inline_function bool rspin_trylock(FAR rspinlock_t *lock)
761: {
762:   rspinlock_t new_val;
763:   rspinlock_t old_val;
764:   int         cpu = this_cpu() + 1;
765:   bool        ret = false;
766: 
767:   /* Already owned this lock. */
768: 
769:   old_val.val = atomic_read(&lock->val);
770: 
771:   if (old_val.owner == cpu)
772:     {
773:       lock->count += 1;
774:       ret = true;
775:     }
776:   else if (old_val.val == 0)
777:     {
778:       /* Try seize the ownership of the lock using CAS. */
779: 
780:       new_val.count = 1;
781:       new_val.owner = cpu;
782: 
783:       ret = atomic_cmpxchg_acquire(&lock->val,
784:                                    &old_val.val,
785:                                    new_val.val);
786: 
787:       /* Mark locked when the lock is successfully acquired. */
788: 
789:       if (ret)
790:         {
791:           spinlock_mark_locked(&lock->info);
792:         }
793:     }
794: 
795:   return ret;
796: }

808:       (l)->count++; \

810:       true; \
811:     })

1009:  * Name: rspin_unlock_irqrestore/rspin_unlock_irqrestore_nopreempt
1010:  *
1011:  * Description:
1012:  *   Nest supported spinunlock, can support UINT16_MAX max depth.
1013:  *   Should work with rspin_lock_irqsave_nopreempt().
1014:  *   Similar feature with leave_critical_section, but isolate by instance.
1015:  *
1016:  *   If SPINLOCK is enabled:
1017:  *     Will release spinlock each cpu last call.
1018:  *
1019:  *   If SPINLOCK is not enabled:
1020:  *     Equivalent to sched_unlock() + up_irq_restore().
1021:  *     Will only sched_unlock once when last called.
1022:  *
1023:  * Input Parameters:
1024:  *   lock - Caller specific rspinlock_s.
1025:  *
1026:  *   flags - The architecture-specific value that represents the state of
1027:  *           the interrupts prior to the call to
1028:  *           spin_unlock_irqrestore_nopreempt(lock);
1029:  *
1030:  * Returned Value:
1031:  *   true  - Indicates exiting the spinlock.
1032:  *
1033:  ****************************************************************************/

1035: #ifdef CONFIG_SPINLOCK
1036: static inline_function
1037: bool rspin_unlock(FAR rspinlock_t *lock)
1038: {
1039:   bool ret = false;
1040: 
1041:   DEBUGASSERT(lock->owner == this_cpu() + 1);
1042:   DEBUGASSERT(lock->count >= 1);
1043: 
1044:   if (--lock->count == 0)
1045:     {
1046:       spinlock_mark_unlocked(&lock->info);
1047:       atomic_set_release(&lock->val, 0);
1048:       ret = true;
1049:     }
1050: 
1051:   return ret;
1052: }

1055: void rspin_unlock_irqrestore(FAR rspinlock_t *lock, irqstate_t flags)
1056: {
1057:   if (rspin_unlock(lock))
1058:     {
1059:       up_irq_restore(flags);
1060:     }
1061: 
1062:   /* If not last rspinlock restore,  up_irq_restore should not required */
1063: }
1064: #else
1065: static inline_function
1066: void rspin_unlock_irqrestore(FAR rspinlock_t *lock, irqstate_t flags)
1067: {
1068:   if (--lock->count == 0)
1069:     {
1070:       lock->owner = 0;
1071:       up_irq_restore(flags);
1072:     }
1073: 
1074:   /* If not last rspinlock restore,  up_irq_restore should not required */
1075: }

1083:     } \
1084:   while (0)

1158: /****************************************************************************
1159:  * Name: read_lock
1160:  *
1161:  * Description:
1162:  *   If this task does not already hold the spinlock, then loop until the
1163:  *   spinlock is successfully locked.
1164:  *
1165:  *   This implementation is non-reentrant and set a bit of lock.
1166:  *
1167:  *  The reader's priority is higher than the writer's priority.  If a reader
1168:  *  holds the lock, a new reader can get its lock but a writer can't get this
1169:  *  lock.
1170:  *
1171:  * Input Parameters:
1172:  *   lock - A reference to the spinlock object to lock.
1173:  *
1174:  * Returned Value:
1175:  *   None.  When the function returns, the spinlock was successfully locked
1176:  *   by this CPU.
1177:  *
1178:  * Assumptions:
1179:  *   Not running at the interrupt level.
1180:  *
1181:  ****************************************************************************/
1182: 
1183: static inline_function void read_lock(FAR volatile rwlock_t *lock)
1184: {
1185:   nxsched_critmon_busywait(true, return_address(0));
1186:   while (true)
1187:     {
1188:       int old = atomic_read(&lock->lock);
1189: 
1190:       if (old > RW_SP_WRITE_LOCKED &&
1191:           atomic_cmpxchg_acquire(&lock->lock, &old, old + 1))
1192:         {
1193:           break;
1194:         }
1195:     }
1196: 
1197:   nxsched_critmon_busywait(false, return_address(0));
1198: }

1200: /****************************************************************************
1201:  * Name: read_trylock
1202:  *
1203:  * Description:
1204:  *   If this task does not already hold the spinlock, then try to get the
1205:  * lock.
1206:  *
1207:  *   This implementation is non-reentrant and set a bit of lock.
1208:  *
1209:  *  The reader's priority is higher than the writer's priority.  If a reader
1210:  *  holds the lock, a new reader can get its lock but a writer can't get this
1211:  *  lock.
1212:  *
1213:  * Input Parameters:
1214:  *   lock - A reference to the spinlock object to lock.
1215:  *
1216:  * Returned Value:
1217:  *   false   - Failure, the spinlock was already locked
1218:  *   true    - Success, the spinlock was successfully locked
1219:  *
1220:  * Assumptions:
1221:  *   Not running at the interrupt level.
1222:  *
1223:  ****************************************************************************/
1224: 
1225: static inline_function bool read_trylock(FAR volatile rwlock_t *lock)
1226: {
1227:   bool ret = false;
1228: 
1229:   while (true)
1230:     {
1231:       int old = atomic_read(&lock->lock);
1232: 
1233:       if (old <= RW_SP_WRITE_LOCKED)
1234:         {
1235:           DEBUGASSERT(old == RW_SP_WRITE_LOCKED);
1236:           break;
1237:         }
1238:       else if (atomic_cmpxchg_acquire(&lock->lock, &old, old + 1))
1239:         {
1240:           ret = true;
1241:           break;
1242:         }
1243:     }
1244: 
1245:   return ret;
1246: }

1248: /****************************************************************************
1249:  * Name: read_unlock
1250:  *
1251:  * Description:
1252:  *   Release a bit on a non-reentrant spinlock.
1253:  *
1254:  * Input Parameters:
1255:  *   lock - A reference to the spinlock object to unlock.
1256:  *
1257:  * Returned Value:
1258:  *   None.
1259:  *

1272: /****************************************************************************
1273:  * Name: write_lock
1274:  *
1275:  * Description:
1276:  *   If this CPU does not already hold the spinlock, then loop until the
1277:  *   spinlock is successfully locked.
1278:  *
1279:  *   This implementation is non-reentrant and set all bit on lock to avoid
1280:  *   readers and writers.
1281:  *
1282:  *  The reader's priority is higher than the writer's priority.  If a reader
1283:  *  holds the lock, a new reader can get its lock but a writer can't get this
1284:  *  lock.
1285:  *
1286:  * Input Parameters:
1287:  *   lock - A reference to the spinlock object to lock.
1288:  *
1289:  * Returned Value:
1290:  *   None.  When the function returns, the spinlock was successfully locked
1291:  *   by this CPU.
1292:  *
1293:  * Assumptions:
1294:  *   Not running at the interrupt level.
1295:  *
1296:  ****************************************************************************/
1297: 
1298: static inline_function void write_lock(FAR volatile rwlock_t *lock)
1299: {
1300:   /* Mark that we want to hold lock */
1301: 
1302:   spinlock_mark_locking(&lock->info);
1303:   nxsched_critmon_busywait(true, return_address(0));
1304: 
1305:   while (true)
1306:     {
1307:       atomic_t zero = RW_SP_UNLOCKED;
1308:       if (atomic_cmpxchg_acquire(&lock->lock, &zero, RW_SP_WRITE_LOCKED))
1309:         {
1310:           break;
1311:         }
1312:     }
1313: 
1314:   spinlock_mark_locked(&lock->info);
1315:   nxsched_critmon_busywait(false, return_address(0));
1316: }

1318: /****************************************************************************
1319:  * Name: write_trylock
1320:  *
1321:  * Description:
1322:  *   If this task does not already hold the spinlock, then loop until the
1323:  *   spinlock is successfully locked.
1324:  *
1325:  *   This implementation is non-reentrant and set all bit on lock to avoid
1326:  *   readers and writers.
1327:  *
1328:  *  The reader's priority is higher than the writer's priority.  If a reader
1329:  *  holds the lock, a new reader can get its lock but a writer can't get this
1330:  *  lock.
1331:  *
1332:  * Input Parameters:
1333:  *   lock - A reference to the spinlock object to lock.
1334:  *
1335:  * Returned Value:
1336:  *   false   - Failure, the spinlock was already locked
1337:  *   true    - Success, the spinlock was successfully locked
1338:  *
1339:  * Assumptions:
1340:  *   Not running at the interrupt level.
1341:  *
1342:  ****************************************************************************/

1344: static inline_function bool write_trylock(FAR volatile rwlock_t *lock)
1345: {
1346:   atomic_t zero = RW_SP_UNLOCKED;
1347:   bool ret = atomic_cmpxchg_acquire(&lock->lock, &zero, RW_SP_WRITE_LOCKED);
1348: 
1349:   if (ret)
1350:     {
1351:       spinlock_mark_locked(&lock->info);
1352:     }
1353: 
1354:   return ret;
1355: }

1357: /****************************************************************************
1358:  * Name: write_unlock
1359:  *
1360:  * Description:
1361:  *   Release all bit on a non-reentrant spinlock.
